45	| I12 | Square target sizes holding 90 % of pointing actions: 17.6 / 18.8 / 4.1 / 4.5 cm, and the per-condition shrinks 6.9 / 11.6 / 6.5 / 8.9 % | Accuracy, p. 8 | **blocked** | Not derivable from anything published: it needs the per-trial 2-D endpoints, and Table 3 gives only the mean and SD of the *scalar* distance. The estimator is implemented and validated against its analytic value (`src/pipeline.py:target_size_90`, `→ selftest`, 11.69 cm vs 11.69 cm). Forcing an isotropic-Rayleigh assumption onto Table 3 — my assumption, not the paper's — gives 22.0 cm where the paper says 17.6 cm |
46	| I13 | Average 8.5 % shrink of the target under correction | Future Work, p. 9 | **verified** | Mean of the paper's own four shrink percentages = 8.475 % (`→ check id s2-target-shrink-mean`) |
47	| I14 | Cross-paper comparison with Mayer et al. 2015: errors "4.8, 1.9, 3.7 times larger", IFRC 89.2 % larger than EFRC after correction, and 2015's EFRC 4.9 % larger than IFRC | Model Discussion, p. 6 | **verified** | All five numbers reproduce against the predecessor's Tables 1–2, row *standing 2 m* (`→ check ids s1-ratio-2015-*`, `s1-ifrc-vs-efrc`, `s1-2015-efrc-vs-ifrc`). The recomputation also settles an ambiguity the paper creates: the word "overall" in that sentence can only mean the RealWorld column, not both environments (see mismatch box) |
48	| I15 | Design and sample arithmetic: 7 × 5 = 35 targets, 35 × 6 × 2 = 420 trials, × 20 participants = 8,400 postures, 420 / 4 = 105 per session, 6 × 35 × 2 = 420 in Study 2, grid spacing = screen / (n − 1) | Study Design pp. 3–4 and 7, Apparatus p. 4, Results p. 5 | **verified** | Every count closes exactly (`→ check ids design-*`), including the spacing: 269.4 / 6 = 44.9 cm and 136.2 / 4 = 34.05 cm, which recovers the digit the PDF's text layer drops in "34.cm" |
49	
50	**Counts: 8 verified, 4 partial, 3 blocked, 15 inner-loop components.**
51	
52	> *Derived rate, not a headline.* 8/15 verified and 12/15 at least partially
53	> reproduced. That number is a summary of **this** decomposition and nothing
54	> else. Slice the pipeline differently — treat "the model" as one component
55	> instead of the four rows I1, I4, I5, I6 — and the same audit yields a
56	> different fraction from the same findings. It is not comparable to another
57	> paper's rate, or to another run's rate on this paper. The table above is the
58	> comparable artifact.

content:
The repository runs standalone from the output directory. Here's what the audit found.

## The paper

Mayer, Schwind, Schweigert & Henze, *The Effect of Offset Correction and Cursor on Mid-Air Pointing in Real and Virtual Environments*, CHI '18 ([10.1145/3173574.3174227](https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174227)). Two lab studies: 20 people point at a 7×5 target grid in a real room and a VR replica (8,400 postures), a 15-parameter quartic is fitted to cancel the systematic offset, then 16 new people validate it in a 2×2×2 selection task.

## Verdict: partial

**Boundary.** 15 inner-loop components (ray-cast geometry → offsets → polynomial fits → LOOCV → the ANOVAs and every derived percentage), 7 outer-loop components (the two studies, raw TLX, eye-dominance screening, anthropometry, consent, recruitment) — never attempted, never simulated, never scored.

**Per-component table: 8 verified, 4 partial, 3 blocked.** The rate is stated in the repo only as a derived footnote to the table, explicitly non-comparable across papers or runs.

**What reproduced.** Everything the paper derives from its own tables — all 35 checkable derivations, including the 29.3 % headline correction, the 13.1 % / 4.5 % Study-2 improvements, and the cross-paper ratios against the 2015 predecessor (which also pinned down that the paper's word "overall" there can only mean the RealWorld column). Equation 1's basis reconstructs exactly as the complete bivariate quartic, and the paper's odd "nonlinear least-squares solver" choice is verified harmless (solvers agree to 6.5 × 10⁻¹⁰).

**What blocked.** No data, and — the sharpest finding — **not one of the ~240 fitted coefficients was ever published**, so the paper's stated contribution cannot be applied by a reader. The predecessor paper did print its coefficients; I re-implemented those in `src/mayer2015_model.py` to show what is missing.

**Mismatches.** 6 of 20 reported *F*/*p* pairs fail recomputation, including a main effect the paper calls significant: `ENVIRONMENT` on accuracy, *F*(1,15) = 1.3, *p* = .027, where that *F* gives *p* = .272. Study 2's fatigue ANOVA reports *F*(5,15) where its own design implies *F*(5,75).

**Artifacts.** 22 locations searched and logged. Two footnote artifacts (marker mounts, hand meshes) are alive after eight years; no code, data, license, or preregistration exists. ACM DL and ResearchGate returned HTTP 403 and are recorded as blocked rather than as absence.

The inner loop is implemented and actually run (`./run_all.sh`, output recorded in `results/run_log.txt`); `src/check_paper.py` needs no data at all and is what produced the mismatch findings.

and it is blocked by the absent file, not by the absent hardware.

### What a follow-up human study would have to cover

Stated plainly, so that the scope of what this audit does *not* establish is not
left to inference. To put the paper's claims back on evidence, a new study would
have to re-collect O1 through O7 in full — nothing in `src/` substitutes for any
of it:

1. **Both samples, not one.** A modelling sample (O1: ~20 participants × 420
   feedback-free pointing gestures at a 35-target grid from 2 m, counterbalanced
   across RealWorld and VirtualReality) *and* a separate validation sample (O2:
   ~16 **new** participants in the 2 × 2 × 2 CORRECTION × CURSOR × ENVIRONMENT
   selection task). Reusing one sample for both would forfeit exactly the
   external validity the paper's second study exists to establish.
2. **The apparatus the measures presuppose.** Marker-based 6DOF tracking of the
   head, both shoulders, upper arm, forearm, hand root and index finger, an HMD,
   and a projector aligned to the same virtual scene — because the dependent
   variable is a ray-screen intersection, not a click. `instrument.json`
   → `servability` names, per component, which of the six criteria this fails
   and why none of it is browser-servable.
3. **The per-participant instrumentation.** The 14 anthropometric measurements
   and the avatar fitted from them (O5), plus eye-dominance screening (O4) — and
   this time a stated decision on what the screening is *for*, since in the
   paper it is measured and then enters no model (D17).
4. **The subjective and procedural layer.** Raw NASA-TLX after every session in
   both studies (O3), informed consent and demographics (O6), and a specified
   recruitment and eligibility procedure (O7) — right-handedness and "no
   locomotor coordination problems" need an instrument, not an adjective.
5. **The twenty decisions of §3, fixed in advance.** A re-run that leaves D1–D20
   open reproduces the paper's ambiguity rather than its result. The four marked
   *High* — LOOCV granularity (D5), the angle reference frame (D7), the recorded
   endpoint instant (D10) and the target-size estimator (D15) — change the
   headline numbers on their own.
6. **The release the original lacks.** Postures, trials, fitted coefficients and

and it is blocked by the absent file, not by the absent hardware.

### What a follow-up human study would have to cover

Stated plainly, so that the scope of what this audit does *not* establish is not
left to inference. To put the paper's claims back on evidence, a new study would
have to re-collect O1 through O7 in full — nothing in `src/` substitutes for any
of it:

1. **Both samples, not one.** A modelling sample (O1: ~20 participants × 420
   feedback-free pointing gestures at a 35-target grid from 2 m, counterbalanced
   across RealWorld and VirtualReality) *and* a separate validation sample (O2:
   ~16 **new** participants in the 2 × 2 × 2 CORRECTION × CURSOR × ENVIRONMENT
   selection task). Reusing one sample for both would forfeit exactly the
   external validity the paper's second study exists to establish.
2. **The apparatus the measures presuppose.** Marker-based 6DOF tracking of the
   head, both shoulders, upper arm, forearm, hand root and index finger, an HMD,
   and a projector aligned to the same virtual scene — because the dependent
   variable is a ray-screen intersection, not a click. `instrument.json`
   → `servability` names, per component, which of the six criteria this fails
   and why none of it is browser-servable.
3. **The per-participant instrumentation.** The 14 anthropometric measurements
   and the avatar fitted from them (O5), plus eye-dominance screening (O4) — and
   this time a stated decision on what the screening is *for*, since in the
   paper it is measured and then enters no model (D17).
4. **The subjective and procedural layer.** Raw NASA-TLX after every session in
   both studies (O3), informed consent and demographics (O6), and a specified
   recruitment and eligibility procedure (O7) — right-handedness and "no
   locomotor coordination problems" need an instrument, not an adjective.
5. **The twenty decisions of §3, fixed in advance.** A re-run that leaves D1–D20
   open reproduces the paper's ambiguity rather than its result. The four marked
   *High* — LOOCV granularity (D5), the angle reference frame (D7), the recorded
   endpoint instant (D10) and the target-size estimator (D15) — change the
   headline numbers on their own.
6. **The release the original lacks.** Postures, trials, fitted coefficients and
   analysis code. Without the coefficients in particular (I5), a validated model
   is still a model nobody else can apply.

What such a study would settle, and this audit cannot: whether people really do
point differently in VR, whether the correction genuinely buys 13.1 % without a
cursor, and whether a cursor really trades ~0.2 s of selection time for
~5 cm of accuracy. This repository takes no position on any of the three.

**What changed:** `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` §2 now ends with an explicit subsection, *What a follow-up human study would have to cover* — six numbered requirements (both samples rather than one reused sample; the tracking apparatus the dependent variable presupposes; the per-participant instrumentation, including a stated purpose for the eye-dominance screening that currently enters no model; the subjective and procedural layer; the twenty §3 decisions fixed in advance, with the four *High*-sensitivity ones called out; and the release the original lacks). The human studies were not attempted, not simulated, and not scored.
